reader.decision: Lower BOUNCE_RETRY_LIMIT from 12 to 3 in mailer/config.py now. Do not build hard/soft bounce classification at this point. Then move on to the cutover date item.
reader.decision_reason: The config change stops the sender block (5 bounces/hour/recipient, 24h block) with no new mechanism. Four bounces stay under the threshold. The classifier needs code that does not exist today, and the message says it only becomes primary when many recipients have dead mailboxes, which is not stated to be the case.

reconstruction.problem: handle_bounce retries a bounced mail up to 12 times, 60 seconds apart. smtp-mx-2 blocks the sender after more than 5 bounces to one recipient in one hour.
reconstruction.what_breaks: One dead mailbox (e.g. Oskar Brandt's) causes more than 5 bounces within about 5 minutes. smtp-mx-2 then blocks invoices@mail.larkspur.io for 24 hours, so every other customer's invoice is delayed and the remaining retries are refused.
reconstruction.fix: Change BOUNCE_RETRY_LIMIT from 12 to 3 in mailer/config.py. This gives 4 bounces total, then message.mark_failed(). The alternative is classifying hard vs soft bounces by SMTP reply code and failing hard bounces at once.
reconstruction.cost: The config change is a one-line edit, but a soft bounce from a busy server now fails after about 3 minutes instead of 12. It is unverified whether attempt starts at 0 or 1, though 3 is safe either way. The classifier would need new code to parse SMTP reply codes, which docs/mail-provider.md says does not exist today.

reader.closing_answer: BOUNCE_RETRY_LIMIT drops to 3. Revisit hard/soft classification only if many recipients turn out to have dead mailboxes.
